summary: Build practical wildlife management skills in surveys, habitat assessment, monitoring, and conservation planning. Enquire about the five-day course.
lede: Wildlife management uses field evidence to guide decisions about species, habitats, and conservation actions. This course is for wildlife officers, protected-area managers, ecological consultants, and conservation project leads who need to plan surveys, assess populations and habitat pressures, and prioritize responses to threats and human-wildlife conflict. It develops practical skills in survey design, population indicators, GIS-based habitat mapping, threat registers, and adaptive monitoring plans.
audienceIntro: Wildlife Management Training suits professionals who collect ecological evidence, coordinate conservation operations, manage wildlife risks, or advise decision-makers on species and habitat outcomes.
prerequisites: Prior experience in conservation, ecology, environmental planning, protected-area operations, or field data collection is useful but not mandatory. You should be comfortable reading basic tables and maps. No programming is required. Advanced topics such as population viability analysis, AI-assisted image classification, and automated monitoring dashboards are taught at conceptual awareness and operational application levels, while survey design, threat registers, GIS exercises, and management planning receive hands-on treatment. Bring a laptop if possible.
